preconditions: W: explicitly invoked guarded payload hashing in an active consumption window; owned temporary inputs. Allocation/read failures are labelled injections, not native host-quota or OOM measurements.

R: explicit operational outcome adapter; real guarded inputs. Permission and file-descriptor refusals use owned isolated POSIX processes. A native address-space-refused allocation is injected as an indivisible initializer, not claimed as the actual SHA-256 memory requirement.
steps: Hash a real 32 MiB attachment with 64 KiB and 4 KiB reusable buffers; bind the complete byte count and independent incremental SHA-256.
Exercise smaller pre-read buffer allocation alternatives, short reads, exact control positions, guarded descriptor lifetime and unchanged critical fixture bytes on failure.
Compare complete hashes across 1-byte through 64-KiB buffers and finite actual allocation attempts; never turn a soft target into a capacity blocker.

Check machine-readable native resource blockers, raw API compatibility, no partial digest or automatic retry after a read, privacy of diagnostics and exact preservation of owned critical fixture bytes.

oracle.requirement_contract: Vor bekannten großen Speicher- und Stagingallokationen MUSS SpecRoad die sparsame Alternative und tatsächliche Verfügbarkeit nach Anhang O.3 prüfen.
oracle.scope: The actual bounded bytearray allocation is attempted before payload consumption; an injected allocation MemoryError halves the requested capacity down to one byte, with a finite stop if the minimum fails. A failure after input consumption is never silently retried. Actual reserved payload capacity is registered separately from measured RSS and released from active ownership on success/failure. A real owned 32 MiB file is read with one observed reusable buffer; tracemalloc bounds the selected Python allocation window below 2 MiB. Full-payload copy, claimed host quota, staging availability or whole-product completion is not inferred. R adds fingerprint_file_outcome with complete fingerprints or observed Code-5 resource/access blockers: failed stage, finite buffer attempts, required remedy, no checkpoint or automatic retry. Safety/invalid-input/programming failures retain their separate exceptions. Only an actually failed one-byte reservation supplies a known minimum; indivisible initializer/read/guard steps do not invent a byte minimum. Original W cases remain unchanged. 6.e.C consolidates growth counting and exact-size digest completion for the existing read/readinto adapters. Their call ordering, fingerprint type, allocation alternatives, raw exceptions and operational blocker reports retain the unchanged W/R behavior contracts; no additional consumer or platform completion is claimed.

open_items: Explicit guarded payload hashing and its operational outcome adapter only; no new CLI command or persistent resume engine. Known-limit integration, staging capacity/reserves, all archive/import/snapshot consumers and full runtime/platform acceptance remain open. Tests distinguish injected errors, native permission/descriptor refusals and the labelled injected indivisible initializer with a real refused allocation. No actual SHA-256 minimum memory benchmark, total RSS, host quota guarantee or recovery from an uncatchable process kill is claimed.
